scenes.title: HOTTER THAN THE SUN
vo: Lightning is five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
So how does it get that hot, and why the boom?

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: Inside a storm cloud, rising air smashes ice and small hail together.
Light ice turns positive and rides up. Heavy hail turns negative and sinks.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: Air is an insulator: it holds the charges apart until the difference gets too big.
Then it fails all at once, in one giant spark.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: One flash carries about a hundred million volts.
Its energy heats the air in its path in a few millionths of a second, to fifty thousand degrees Fahrenheit.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: Air heated that fast explodes outward, like a popping balloon.
That bang is what we call thunder.

scenes.title: AFTERMATH
vo: That heat starts about ten thousand forest fires a year.

scenes.title: AFTERMATH
vo: And lightning killed about twenty-seven Americans a year from two thousand nine to twenty eighteen.
